The only light left in town is a tiny corner shop. And something is standing in its door.
Last time, the shadow said Mia's name. In Mia's voice.

text: Mia grabs your hand. You run.

Past frozen people, to the only lit sign in town. Open twenty-four hours.
Through the glass you see it. One phone charger, glowing by the till.
Your battery, two percent. Mia's, one.
Then the static slides in front of the door. It doesn't move. It just waits.
Your phone buzzes. A text from your own number. Don't let her phone die.

text: Too late. Mia's screen goes black. Zero percent.
And Mia freezes, mid-step, just like everyone else.
Would you walk past it to reach the charger? Yes or no.
